utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. Good morning to everyone in and around the courtroom. This is case IT-08-91-T, the Prosecutor versus Mico Stanisic and Stojan Zupljanin.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Registrar. Good morning to everyone. May we have the appearances for today, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. On behalf of the Prosecution, Alexis Demirdjian, with Joanna Korner, and Case Manager Crispian Smith.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Your Honours. For Mr. Stanisic, Mr. Cvijetic, Tatjana Savic, Ms. Deirdre Montgomery, and Dominic Kennedy.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. For Zupljanin Defence, Igor Pantelic and Dragan Krgovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Thank you. And if there is nothing to delay us, I would invite Mr. Cvijetic to commence his cross-examination. But before that I remind the witness that you're still on your oath, sir. Yes, Mr. Cvijetic.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone for the counsel, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Give me a moment, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Mr. Petrovic.

utterances.speaker: OBREN PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: My name is Slobodan Cvijetic, and I am counsel on the Stanisic Defence team. I will have a couple of questions for you. I will start where you left off yesterday, which was the procedure for your removal from the post of the chief of police station; is that right?

utterances.speaker: OBREN PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Yesterday you detailed the reasons behind your removal, and you described for us how this all came about. What I still find unclear, Mr. Petrovic, is what sort of procedure was actually initiated against you, with a view to removing you from your post? We have the complete Bench today, so could you please, for their benefit, briefly describe this for us again, loud and clear. And can you please emphasise the various documents you received leading up to your removal. Have I made myself clear?

utterances.speaker: OBREN PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Can we hear how it was that you came to be removed from your post.

utterances.speaker: OBREN PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that it was after the meeting held in October, organised by Colonel Lisica, that I was removed. I reviewed the document, though I don't have it now. Later on, the letter was sent to the Security Services Centre, since Mr. Andrija Bjelosevic was at this meeting too, as were representatives of the municipality and deputies of the Republika Srpska National Assembly, as far as I understood the matter.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: What still remains unclear to me is the nature of the document you seem to be referring to. In the interviews with ICTY investigators, which were held a while ago, you said in those interviews that these documents exist -- or the document exists and that it can be found.

utterances.speaker: OBREN PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I don't have the document, but an individual showed me this proposal of the CSB addressed to the ministry, detailing the reasons for my removal. It is a customary practice that if there are reasons for your removal, then the chief of the centre would issue a proposal to the minister for your removal, and this is what was done in my case.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Did you receive the document on your removal from the minister?

utterances.speaker: OBREN PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did, a dispatch.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Do you have that dispatch?

utterances.speaker: OBREN PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do. I gave it to the investigators.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Do you recall the date the decision bears?

utterances.speaker: OBREN PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was in early January 1993.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Could that have been the 18th of January, 1993?

utterances.speaker: OBREN PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [No verbal response]

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Can you repeat your answer; it is not entered in the transcript.

utterances.speaker: OBREN PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's possible.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Mr. Cvijetic, can you assist us, please. Is this -- how is this going to be of assistance to the Chamber at the end of the exercise? Where are we going?

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, if you haven't forgotten, the witness stated yesterday that he was removed because he was assisting the Muslims. You will recall that as the second reason for his removal he cited his protection of Muslims. And I want to show that this isn't true because both he and the police station he was in charge of did not achieve the results as expected in that period and that was the reason why he was removed, and not because he had allegedly helped Muslims.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Can't you challenge him directly on this? Wouldn't it be of greater assistance if, that being your case, you move directly to -- to that point?

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, the witness doesn't have a single argument lending support to what he says, and that's why I have taken this road, and this is how I've approached the matter, and, by your leave, I should like to proceed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Mr. Cvijetic, I'm sorry, the point that you're trying to make is -- is clear enough. I would concur with the Presiding Judge, that you should just get at it straight away. But the underlying question is really why and just how is it relevant that the witness was dismissed for whatever reason [Microphone not activated]. What -- what kind of assistance will that bring to -- to the trial against your client?

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I cannot but recall the transcript of -- of the witness's testimony yesterday. He spent a great deal of time explaining that he was removed because he had helped Muslims. And you know that the indictment charges the clients with discriminatory intent in relation to non-Serbs. And if this is why he was removed, this is a qualification that could be taken against our clients by Their Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Your Honours. If I may be of any assistance, I believe that this is a relevant topic actually to the matters at hand. Our theory of the case is that this individual was removed in his assistance, as he said, of Muslims and that measures were not taken against other police chiefs who bore more criminal responsibility. So I believe that this might be a relevant one -- examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: We do appreciate that, Mr. Demirdjian and Mr. Cvijetic. Our only question is, Why isn't it -- why don't you -- why doesn't counsel move directly to it rather than take this circuitous route? That's the only question that we have. We fully understand what the challenge is.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, nothing easier for me, Your Honours, than to say -- to put to the witness that he is lying. But I haven't done so in relation to any of the witnesses because my jurisdiction prohibits me from doing so. In my jurisdiction, one needs to present documents to the witness that prove the opposite, and -- and this is the basis on which the Chamber will examine the matter. If you prefer me to do so, I can put to the witness that he is lying and just leave the matter at that. But will this convince the Trial Chamber that the witness, indeed, is lying?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. Cvijetic; but, if possible, short -- short-circuit your route. That's the only thing we're asking.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I understand, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Witness, according to what you say, the help you provided to the Muslims consisted of the fact that at the start of the war you set up a multi-ethnic unit comprising Muslims as well. Now, you also stated that these Muslims that you included in your unit simply dispersed and fled as attacked by the army and you said that this was taken -- held against you.

utterances.speaker: OBREN PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I didn't say that this was taken against me. I set up this unit at Sevarlije, but when this paramilitary unit or whoever it was captured Sevarlije, they attacked the policemen and they simply took their uniforms and weapons and crossed to the Federation.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: But you said to the investigators that this was the reason why you were removed, that somebody thought of this incident at the end of the year and cited this as the reason.

utterances.speaker: OBREN PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I only said that there was a proposal from the centre for my removal. Now, if you -- I did say that among the reasons cited, there was also the reason that I failed to enforce law and order. But one of these bullet points also included the fact that I mentioned. If you -- perhaps the best method would be to speak to the former chief of the centre. You see, I think a year ago I saw this man who showed me the very document that was sent to the minister.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: I put it to you that this document does not mention Muslims or any sort of assistance you may have provided them at all; rather what is mentioned is only the -- your failure to achieve any of the tasks that were presented to the police station. What -- what you state to substantiate your claims is merely the fact that you set up this multi-ethnic unit in Sevarlije which dispersed when exposed to an attack from the army and crossed to the side of the Federation. Or is it, perhaps -- so can you please tell us, Is it because what you did in April that you were removed at the end of that same year? Was it somebody thought back about those events?

utterances.speaker: OBREN PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, you see, by that time, the police force had not yet been fully formed --

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Can you just answer my question. Was this the reason you think why you were removed?

utterances.speaker: OBREN PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If you can't signed the document in the Ministry of Interior, I will locate the document which is entitled proposal for my removal.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Very well. You haven't managed to persuade me of what you say, but I will try to give you my view of the matter. Do you know that the minister of the interior issued rules governing disciplinary responsibility of the MUP staff of the Serbian Republic of --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Mr. Cvijetic, you're referring to events in April. What are you -- what events are you referring to?

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I'm quoting the words of the witness who says that earlier on in the war he established a multi-ethnic unit comprising Muslims and that at Sevarlije, as has just been said, when they came under attack of another unit, he mentioned it, the Muslims crossed over to the other side with their weapons and equipment and that that was the reason why he was removed later, because that was interpreted as his helping the Muslims. That is his statement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Okay, thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Your Honours, let me just place an objection on the record also with the way the question was asked. Mr. Cvijetic, you haven't managed to persuade me of that. I don't think it is fair for a witness to be put that type of pressure of having to persuade the Defence. These type of comments are inappropriate in our view.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: I -- I did hear that statement, but I thought it was just the way of his phrasing it, and I let it pass, Mr. Demirdjian.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Mr. Petrovic, do you know that the minister of the interior adopted a regulation on the disciplinary accountability of the employees of the MUP of the Serbian Republic and wartime conditions?

utterances.speaker: OBREN PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we please see 1D54. I'm afraid that the document is visible only on half the screen. We won't be able to enlarge it. Could we please change that. Could we just see the English version too. I think this is the correct page in the Serbian version, but I don't think the English page is right. This seems to be the title page only. We have to go one further. Could we please zoom in.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Can you read this first page, Mr. Petrovic?

utterances.speaker: OBREN PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Here you can see that the minister, while this -- these circumstances were -- prevailed, established disciplinary responsibility of MUP staff. And the CSB chiefs, administration chiefs in the ministry, and police detachment commanders took over the function of the first instances disciplinary organ. It goes on to say that the Ministry of Interior will rule on appeals. Can you see that? It's in the second paragraph.

utterances.speaker: OBREN PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can see that.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Let us go to the first page of the document.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Actually, in the following page of the document.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: In these provisions, especially in Article 2, it --

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we display Article 2 in the English version, please; it's on the next page. Could we please turn to the following page in English, where a list of these serious violations can be found.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Until we were shown that, sir, here's a list of serious violations of work duty and those which are characterised as lighter violations, or less serious violations. Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: OBREN PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Under Article 4 --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Sorry, interpreter's correction: 3.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Which is on the following page in both linguistic versions, it seems. Let us just scroll down so we can see Article 3 in English.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Here's a list of disciplinary measures that can be imposed for violating a work duty. Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: OBREN PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: And here's an admonition, public admonition, and transfer to other jobs for up to 12 years, fines, and termination of employment. Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: OBREN PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Article 4 says that the chief of the CSB, among others, imposes disciplinary measures for serious violations of work duty. And it's the chief of the SJB who does so for minor violations. Article 5 reads that the procedure can be initiated by any MUP staff. Do you understand that?

utterances.speaker: OBREN PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: The following provisions describe the procedure for -- actually, the disciplinary procedure is outlined, where, in the first instance, the parties have to be heard, and then a measure will be taken. Mr. Petrovic, according to these rules, you could have been removed from your position pursuant to the decision of the chief of the CSB. And that decision -- or, rather, you could appeal that decision by filing an appeal to the minister who is a second-instance body. Was it that way?

utterances.speaker: OBREN PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it probably was. But I was removed, pursuant to a dispatch. There was no disciplinary procedure involved. That's it.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: You're saying that you saw that dispatch and that it says that the minister is removing you.

utterances.speaker: OBREN PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's what it says. And it finishes by saying that disciplinary procedure shall be initiated or something like that.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Is the reason for your removal stated?

utterances.speaker: OBREN PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it isn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I would now like to deal with that dispatch. Could we, therefore, see a document that -- or whose translation we have been waiting for. It is 1D03-3251. 1D03- -- yes, this is it.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Mr. Petrovic.

utterances.speaker: OBREN PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: This is the dispatch. Can you identify it?

utterances.speaker: OBREN PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Is it true that this is the very dispatch?

utterances.speaker: OBREN PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: I'll read the text. I'll ask the interpreters to interpret. It's very short. We sent it for translation, but it isn't done yet. The heading reads: Ministry of Internal Affairs, Bijeljina. And then there is a number which is barely legible, but the date, as you said, is the 18th of January, 1993. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: OBREN PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: The document was sent to the CSB of Doboj; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: OBREN PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: It goes on to say: "Reference, your dispatch number 13/93." And then the date isn't really legible. But it is clear that the year is 1993. Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: OBREN PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: In paragraph 1, Mr. Stanisic says: "Pursuant to your proposal concerning Milorad Novakovic, a decision has been adopted to the effect that, as of 15 January 1993, he is appointed to the position of chief of SJB Doboj." Have I read this out correctly?

utterances.speaker: OBREN PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: In the following line, we can see that it says: "The decision will be sent to you by regular mail." And the last paragraph reads: "As for the shortcomings in the work of the earlier chief of SJB Doboj, Obren Petrovic, you shall act in accordance with the provisions of the rules of disciplinary accountability." And, finally, it is signed: "Minister of the Interior, Mico Stanisic." Have I read out this dispatch correctly?

utterances.speaker: OBREN PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Mr. Petrovic, with regard to you and any other staff of the ministry, the minister implemented the rules that he passed himself, as well as the law. And as we see, he didn't remove you, nor had -- did he have the authority to do so. On the contrary. He demands that the rules be applied in order to establish your possible accountability, and he doesn't even go into the reasons for your removal. Is this what this dispatch says?

utterances.speaker: OBREN PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's what it says.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: It follows that the minister was in a position to learn about your problem only if you were to appeal the disciplinary measure of transfer to another position or termination of employment. And only then would he possibly consider the reasons for your removal. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: OBREN PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, that's how it should have been.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: It follows from this that up until January 18th the disciplinary file hadn't even made it to the minister because he demands that this be done to enable him to act. Furthermore, the only thing you hold against the minister -- he said he may have listened to you as a human, as a -- as a person, right?

utterances.speaker: OBREN PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: And here's what I put to you: The minister cannot violate the rules; and being the second-instance disciplinary body, he is not allowed to anticipate the outcome of the disciplinary procedure in the first instance. So he cannot even hear you until your appeal and your file come to his desk. Mr. Petrovic, you will agree with me, won't you, that the minister doesn't deal with your cooperation with the Muslims or your help to the Muslims here. Does that -- isn't that what follows from this -- from this document?

utterances.speaker: OBREN PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. This -- what you said cannot be found in the document.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Mr. Petrovic, you told us that, practically speaking, you didn't lose your job within the police force; you were just transferred to a different job.

utterances.speaker: OBREN PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: What tasks did you receive?

utterances.speaker: OBREN PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Inspector for aliens.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Until when you first stayed at the police force?

utterances.speaker: OBREN PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Until the 4th of May, 1993.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Did you continue working after that date? Were you in the police force in 1994?

utterances.speaker: OBREN PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the 27th of May. So, more than a year later. 27th of May 1994, I've started working again.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Who received you back into the police force in 1994? Who was at the head of the MUP at the time when you were received back?

utterances.speaker: OBREN PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: In a conversation, you told me that you remembered that Mr. Stanisic was appointed for the minister of the interior in 1994, and that he even appointed you as a commander of a PJP unit.

utterances.speaker: OBREN PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was appointed, but I wasn't seen by the minister. I didn't have a conversation with him.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: But who appointed you, whose signature was on the document, who appointed you to this PJP unit, commander's position?

utterances.speaker: OBREN PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was based on the proposal of the commander of the centre, Vaso Skondric, and it was the minister who was current minister at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Which one? Which minister?

utterances.speaker: OBREN PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If you say it was Stanisic, then it was Stanisic.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: I want to hear you saying it, that it was Mr. Stanisic.

utterances.speaker: OBREN PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Well, I put it to you that in 1994 Mico Stanisic appointed to you this position. Mr. Petrovic, it is obvious that Mr. Stanisic did not find anything wrong with your assistance to the Muslims and appointed you to your post.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I have a proposal here. Since the witness recognised this document by Mico Stanisic and the documents only needs a translation, I would like to ask for this document to be MFI'd. We will notify the Chamber once the translation is in. It's going to happen very soon. It's a very short document. I have been told the translation will come in today, even.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Yes, so it should be so marked.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit 1D258, marked for identification, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Mr. Petrovic, let us go back to the beginning of your testimony here during the direct examination. I would like to clear up the conditions in Doboj in 1992, and I would like to ask you to help me clear this up.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... before you move on, there's some unclarity in the evidence that you have elicited from the witness. I thought you told us earlier this morning that the real reason why this witness was removed from his position as chief of the SJB in Doboj was not as the witness claimed yesterday, that he had been assisting Muslims, but, rather, for some other reasons. And I understood your questions to be that the real reason was that this witness was inefficient in his role as chief of the SJB. Now, just now, a very short while ago, you came back to the issue of whether or not he had assisted Muslims. And now you used that argument to suggest that, in fact, Stanisic had, all along, been aware of the fact that the witness had been helping Muslims but that he didn't mind. I don't know if I misunderstood you, but if this -- so then there seems to be a contradiction in the two parts of your -- of the evidence that you have received from this witness, so I kindly ask you to clarify.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, what wasn't translated to you, I made an allusion. I said that the minister did not hold it against you, that was an allusion I was making. But what I wanted to say it's obvious that he didn't even know the reasons, the minister. Tanja tells me that it wasn't translated, so I would like to ask this to be entered into the transcript.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Have I made it clear now, Your Honour?

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Mr. Witness, do you remember that I told you that minister obviously did not know even about the reasons? Did I say that?

utterances.speaker: OBREN PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When?

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: When I said that Mr. Stanisic didn't hold it against you and -- because he didn't even know that -- the reason was, just now.

utterances.speaker: OBREN PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know exactly what words you have used.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: At this point counsel is giving evidence here, and he is saying that it wasn't translated. I believe, if we go a few pages up, his comment was translated. He says: "Mr. Petrovic, it is obvious that Mr. Stanisic did not find anything wrong with your assistance to the Muslims and appointed you to your post." And then he moved on to his next question. And that is at page 15, line 15. So I'm just as confused as to where this is going. Because you're giving evidence and not the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Well, of course, the disadvantage that we have is that we hear a question, which is interpreted, we hear an answer that's interpreted, it is only as Mr. Cvijetic has now represented that there is something that wasn't interpreted. So I suggest that if this is what he is saying happened, then the question should be asked again to avoid, as Mr. Demirdjian has just pointed out, the possibility of counsel giving evidence. Sorry, Mr. Pantelic, you had something to add?

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: No, Your Honour, it's just a clarification from transcript. It's page 16, line 24. My learned friend Mr. Cvijetic said "allusion" but not "illusion," so it should be corrected.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. And Tanja is telling me that it was mistranslated, that the second part of my sentence was not translated, the part where I said that he most probably didn't even know about it. This is not my testimony. I'm just putting into the transcript the parts of what I've asked and wasn't entered in. That was all, Your Honours. It was a commentary by me. But the Prosecutor was right, I shouldn't have testified. May I continue, Your Honour?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Yes, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Mr. Petrovic, the town of Doboj is situated in the - let's call it - dark zone that was left out once the corridor was cut?

utterances.speaker: OBREN PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Banja Luka and the Republic of Serbian Krajina was also in that zone?

utterances.speaker: OBREN PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: The town of Doboj is specific because, militarily speaking, it was surrounded by Muslim and Croat forces from the three sides, and you were only in contact with Banja Luka; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: OBREN PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: From what I've gathered from your testimony, the actual physical communication, and also using other modes of communication with other parts of the Republika Srpska and the ministry itself, Doboj established such communication only in late July/beginning of August. Am I right?

utterances.speaker: OBREN PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: In Doboj, under such condition, several units came to -- to Doboj. Major Stankovic; the Red Berets; paramilitary formations getting set there; and also Colonel Lisica shows up, the man who was in command of the operation of breakout?

utterances.speaker: OBREN PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, Colonel Lisica came only later, when the forces started heading towards Brod. Initially it was Talic who was in command. There was Martic's police and all these that you've listed, all the other units.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Major Stankovic destroyed the organisation of the CSB and turns stations of reserve police into detachments?

utterances.speaker: OBREN PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, he created the Doboj police detachment, using the detachments established by him, military detachments, and then he transferred these people, about 300 of them, into the police.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: 1300. Correction, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And because without that we wouldn't have even 200 policemen.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: The use of these very same units in combat activities was something that he was ordering, and he claimed to be the commander of the defence of Doboj. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: OBREN PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, yes. These companies were organised in such a way that they were positioned on front lines towards either Tuzla or Zenica or Jahovac. These were the lines against Croatian forces. He believed that since they were on these lines already, he can subordinate the companies, individual companies. Depending on the operation. For instance, if it was about Grapska, he would take the company that was in the vicinity of Grapska and use it.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: I have a statement from your written statement where you are saying that Red Berets also obeyed his orders. Am I right?

utterances.speaker: OBREN PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, they did obey them.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: You told us yesterday that the Red Berets could resubordinate part of the reserve police using his authority and then use it in combat activities.

utterances.speaker: OBREN PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Based on Stankovic's order, they could have done so.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Did the police have anything to do with paramilitary formations?

utterances.speaker: OBREN PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no, they didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: You claim they didn't. Am I right?

utterances.speaker: OBREN PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, they didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: They didn't have any cooperation with the police -- or, rather, the police with them?

utterances.speaker: OBREN PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, they didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Occasionally they would even surround the CSB building, and you had to ask Major Stankovic to intervene and to have you released?

utterances.speaker: OBREN PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Does that mean that they were under his authority, since they obeyed him?

utterances.speaker: OBREN PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, since they obeyed him, it should mean that he was their commander.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: The question was put to you about who was supplying the Red Berets with weapons and ammunition. You said that it was the army.

utterances.speaker: OBREN PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, the army. They had depots. They also formed detachments. They armed them.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: And then we come to the following question: If all of them were under the authority of the army, how is it possible that this unit of the Red Berets was, for about a month or a month and a half, on the pay list of the CSB? Let me put it to you -- let me put my case to you, and you will tell me whether you think it is possible. The commander of the Red Berets and Major Stankovic could have gone to the part of the service where the pay lists were being made an order for these people to be put on the pay list, and you, in the police, could not say no to that. Am I right?

utterances.speaker: OBREN PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The establishment of the detachments by Stankovic, based on the conclusion of the Crisis Staff that everyone should receive their pay, makes me conclude that people, even people who weren't part of SUP, were receiving salary from us. Even the decision for payment for the month of April --

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Let me just see if everything is in the transcript. Mr. Petrovic, the point I'm trying to make is that the members of the unit commanded by Rajo Bozovic, were never members of the police, that is to say, of the public security centre, in formal and legal terms, that is?

utterances.speaker: OBREN PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, in formal and legal terms, they weren't.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: The fact that they were on the payroll for a month and a half or two is the result of what we've just been discussing and did not confer upon them the status of authorised officials of the Security Services Centre. Am I right?

utterances.speaker: OBREN PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe that you are.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: You said yesterday that the funds for the salaries arrived from Sarajevo; you probably meant the Ministry of Interior. But, in that case, the payroll could not have looked this way, because, after all, they would also then be members of the Ministry of the Interior.

utterances.speaker: OBREN PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, yes. This only lasted for a month or two.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: You also said that the payroll for April is a bit controversial.

utterances.speaker: OBREN PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, because there were different individuals who were on the reserve police force.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Mr. Petrovic, the last question on this topic that I have is a very clear one: The payroll was, in fact, condoned by the Crisis Staff who approved these funds for the payment of salaries?

utterances.speaker: OBREN PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, for the -- the remaining policemen, 250, there were no salaries to be found, not even for the army --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the witness please repeat the last sentence he said. And can the speakers please make a pause.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: The interpreters would wish the -- yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: I will repeat my question, and can you please give us a brief answer. Did -- did the Crisis Staff condone this practice of payrolls by approving funds for the salaries?

utterances.speaker: OBREN PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Mr. Petrovic, in addition to the units that I enumerated, there were several other minor paramilitary formations present in the area. They had different names and various uniforms, did they not?

utterances.speaker: OBREN PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: There was a paramilitary group called Kraljica, Queen; is that right?

utterances.speaker: OBREN PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Preda's Wolves.

utterances.speaker: OBREN PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: There were several units named after their leaders. There was Dragan Ljubicic and several others. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: OBREN PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: You, Mr. Petrovic, were not in conflict with any of these unit, starting from Stankovic to the Green Berets -- the Red Berets and paramilitary formations, you personally. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: OBREN PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I did not particularly agree with them, but I didn't have any physical contacts with them either.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: You have anticipated my next question. The fact that you were not in conflict with them does not necessarily mean that you agreed with them or supported what they did; is that right?

utterances.speaker: OBREN PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not support what they were doing.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Bearing in mind the extent to which the police was engaged in war activities at the time, were you capable of standing up to all these units and their orders, and were you able to prevent their activities, at least for that period of a month and a half?

utterances.speaker: OBREN PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, not. We were not.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Go ahead.

utterances.speaker: OBREN PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because all the police force was deployed to the lines. And I told you how that small number of policemen left behind at the police station fared. They were beaten up too.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: You will agree with me, then, will you not, that, save for the siege from the outside mounted by the Muslim and Croat forces, Doboj also experienced some sort of a siege from within, where the police did not have room for any sort of ordinary policing work; is that right?

utterances.speaker: OBREN PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Based on their geographical location, many of the police stations belonging to the Security Services Centre were under the control of the Croat and Muslim forces so that the very Security Services Centre boiled down to, at best, a public security station of Doboj.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Can the witness repeat his answer, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Mr. Witness, would you please repeat your last answer. The interpreters didn't get it.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] There was Doboj, Teslic, and Petrovo.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: You will agree with me, then, that identical problems existed in Teslic and Petrovo, as in Doboj; is that right?

utterances.speaker: OBREN PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Finally, on -- on this topic, let me say that for all practical intents and purposes the centre in Doboj, with its chief Andrija Bjelosevic, had only you and your station in Doboj, essentially, through which he could have or -- or should have tried to enforce law and order in Doboj; is that right?

utterances.speaker: OBREN PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: You said that in that period of time it was practically impossible because you did not have the necessary clout. Am I right?

utterances.speaker: OBREN PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, we didn't have the clout, and there was the Banja Luka unit that arrived immediately.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: At the time, you could only have received assistance from Banja Luka, and not from the centre at Pale, right?

utterances.speaker: OBREN PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: In that period of time, Mr. Petrovic, you could have engaged in law enforcement activities with how many men exactly? Tell us.

utterances.speaker: OBREN PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't think we had more than 20 policemen at the station.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: With as many policemen, you could not have secured your own station either, could you have?

utterances.speaker: OBREN PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Orders from the chief of the Security Services Centre did reach you, and in these orders he demanded that you take at least some sort of action. And you, within the limits of what was possible, did try and take some measures, did you not?

utterances.speaker: OBREN PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Before the break I have one more question to finish this off, though I think you have already stated this. None of the detention centres existing at the time were under the control of the police; is that right?

utterances.speaker: OBREN PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: You had a small room within your station, but my understanding is that even the individuals you were entitled to hold in custody for up to three days were transferred to the official district prison because the conditions there were better; is that right?

utterances.speaker: OBREN PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: The unlawful activities of unlawful detention from that period of time had nothing to do with the police force, did they?

utterances.speaker: OBREN PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I would now like to move onto a different topic, and I suggest that now would be the right time for the break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: You may continue, Mr. Cvijetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Mr. Petrovic, I will now start showing you some documents I would like you to comment on.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please see 1D00-0700.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Mr. Petrovic, this is a decision of the Crisis Staff of the Serbian municipality of Doboj. As you see, it's dated 15 June 1992; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: OBREN PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: I apologise, the written version was drafted on the 15th of June, but in the first sentence we can see that it is basically a decision taken at a meeting held on the 15th of May, 1992. I made a mistake. Do you agree, is that what it says?

utterances.speaker: OBREN PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's what it says.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: All items are interesting to us. Let us start with number 1. It says: "The chief of the public security station is tasked with ensuring that all decisions and conclusions of the Crisis Staff relating to the public security station are carried out within five days." Mr. Petrovic, this seems to be applying to you, seems to be referring to you. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: OBREN PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: You will agree with me, won't you, when I say that obviously at that moment the Crisis Staff is the highest authority in the territory of Doboj municipality, which means that it can engage in doing your work?

utterances.speaker: OBREN PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, yes. The person signed here is Stankovic, the commander of the defence of the town.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: You actually answered my question -- following question in advance. I was about to ask that the most important decision in town were taken by them, right?

utterances.speaker: OBREN PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: All right. Let's move on to item 2. It says: The Crisis Staff of Doboj municipality requests that the chief of the Doboj Security Centre to give reasons or explain all decisions of the MUP relating to the organisation of the centre and the appointment of personnel there. You will agree with me, won't you, when I say that at that moment, when there was no communication with the ministry, the Crisis Staff started meddling with the work of the ministry, including the appointments at the centre. Is that what follows from this item?

utterances.speaker: OBREN PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it does follow from this decision.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: If we remind ourselves of that information note by Andrija Bjelosevic, the chief, about how his assistant, Milan Savic, was appointed, we see that what he wrote - namely, that he was appointed purpose to a decision of the Crisis Staff - is indeed true. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: OBREN PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Let's pass on to item 3. Again, something for you. It says: "The chief of the public security station is tasked with compiling a list of appointed heads and inspectors and send it to the Crisis Staff for approval." The following paragraph reads: "All appointments at the public security station are considered temporary and shall remain in force until the situation has returned to normal and the combat operations have ended." In other words, the appointments of lower-ranking staff in your station, the Crisis Staff's approval is required. That's what it says, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: OBREN PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's what it says.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Thus, they are, in fact, limiting your legal authority to appoint personnel?

utterances.speaker: OBREN PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Under the law, I should have made a proposal for appointments to the chief, and the chief was supposed to forward that to the minister.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: You will agree with me, won't you, when I say that this actually breaks the decision-making chain in the MUP, doesn't it?

utterances.speaker: OBREN PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Item 4. Here the Crisis Staff orders all groups and individuals who are maintaining law and order in the area of the Serbian municipality of Doboj to place themselves under the command of the chief - and I will give my own account later on - that is, to you. And you are to --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could counsel please repeat the last part?

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: So the Crisis Staff goes on interfering with this decision-making process in the MUP and assigns you tasks, right?

utterances.speaker: OBREN PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Then you are required to submit reports to the Crisis Staff in the next paragraph, right?

utterances.speaker: OBREN PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: And let us not quote every subsequent item. Anyway, all subsequent items relate to the work of the SJBs, and tasks are assigned to it. Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: OBREN PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can see it.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: We didn't hear the last sentence the witness said.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Please repeat the last part of your answer and wait for the interpretation to finish. Say it now.

utterances.speaker: OBREN PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: At the end, they also referred to the municipal prison.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Yes. We've already received information from which it follows that the prison warden submitted reports to the Crisis Staff and made requests to them. Mr. Petrovic, the Crisis Staff, among others, decided that a curfew be imposed in the territory of the Serbian municipality of Doboj in a certain time-period. Am I right?

utterances.speaker: OBREN PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: That decision applied to all citizens except for authorised officials and persons working for bodies of special interest; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: OBREN PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: So the Crisis Staff gives tasks to the police to implement its decision and control its -- its -- control the implementation.

utterances.speaker: OBREN PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: After -- apart from the police, the Red Berets did so and the military police.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please see a document of the Crisis Staff that has to do with this. Your Honours, I apologise. This previous document, as it was recognised by the witness, I will repeat that it is 1D00-0700. I seek to tender it into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Admitted and marked.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit 1D259, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Could we now please see 1D00-47 - correction - 4575. 4575.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Do take a minute to read it so you can comment on it. So, the Crisis Staff adopts a decision on rules governing law and order in the Serbian municipality of Doboj. And in Article 1 it stipulates that moving or loitering outside the permitted hours - and that is three hours a day; I believe it was from 8.00 till 11.00 - in the morning, to get supplies, et cetera, was -- is considered a violation.

utterances.speaker: OBREN PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, the hours changed. Sometimes they would be extended; other times, shortened.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Apart from this, a violation is also staying in public places for a longer time. We don't need to go into the details.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Finally, could we please go to the last page. Can we see Articles 4 and 5 in English. It should be on the following page. Yes, here it's.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: In Article 4, you see that fines are imposed for violations of law and order. You will agree with me, won't you, that there is no distinction made in this decision between citizens based on their ethnicity. So it applied to all citizens, right?

utterances.speaker: OBREN PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: So it also applied to Serbs, didn't it?

utterances.speaker: OBREN PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: I'll ask you, as a police officer with much experience: This measure was motivated by practical and security-related reasons, right?

utterances.speaker: OBREN PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: It wasn't safe to move about Doboj in that period, due to the constant shelling. And this also enabled the police to control the town easier in a certain period, right?

utterances.speaker: OBREN PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Mr. Cvijetic, I noticed that in the title of this document the order seemed to be restricted to the Serbian municipality of Doboj. Since you are raising the issue of the territorial extension of this decision, you might just check this out with the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm afraid I do not understand.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: You --

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I can ask the witness directly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: You raised the issue of whether this issue applied to all citizens, including Serbs. And my comment to that was that since the decision appears to be limited in its territorial extension, then it might be that in the non-Serb part of the Doboj municipality the decision did not bind anyone. Meaning that the decision would only bind people living within the Serbian part of the Doboj municipality, and, of course, it would apply to Serbs living there and possibly also to whichever Muslims or Croats have -- remained. So you are raising, really, the issue of whether or not this decision would apply outside the Serbian part of the Doboj municipality.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, you have answered the question already. But I actually meant the same that you're saying.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: But we can ask the witness to which territory this decision applied and whether it applied to all citizens in the Serbian municipality of Doboj, regardless of their ethnicity.

utterances.speaker: OBREN PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Serbian municipality included the entire town and applied to all citizens.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Regardless of their ethnicity?

utterances.speaker: OBREN PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Regardless of their ethnicity.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, since the witness is familiar with this decision, and, to some extent, he had to implement it, I seek to tender it into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Admitted and marked.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit 1D260, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In the -- oh, shall we call up 1D00-2327, as a follow-up on the document we've looked at before.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone for the counsel, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Mr. Petrovic, this is an order from the chief of the Security Services Centre, Doboj, to the public security station in Doboj, where, in the preamble, it is stated, Due to the increasing number of public complaints regarding raids by persons wearing blue uniforms into homes in Doboj at night, searches conducted without appropriate warrants, harassment, appropriation of money and so on, persons being taken away, the chief hereby orders, under 1, that the public security station in Doboj should gather all the various notices by citizens and other information on these developments and investigate how founded these complaints, indeed, were? Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: OBREN PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: In item 2, the chief orders that control at check-points be stepped up. And goes on to say that while curfew is in force, only official vehicles may move about if they are issued with an appropriate order from an authorised official from the public security centre, or station; whereas, other vehicles should be excluded from traffic and the individuals who were in the vehicle should be taken into custody for as long as the curfew is in force. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: OBREN PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Other measures are also proposed with a view to enforcing law and order, and they are contained in items 3 and 4. We can read them, but I think it's enough to confirm that you can see them here.

utterances.speaker: OBREN PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: I suppose that you did receive this order. It does state you among the addressees.

utterances.speaker: OBREN PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I probably did.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: It was an obligation on your part, and I suppose you did act upon it?

utterances.speaker: OBREN PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: What strikes me here is that not even members of the police station or centre can move about unless they are furnished with appropriate orders or documents. Is that your interpretation of item 2 as well? Can you read it, please.

utterances.speaker: OBREN PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: And you are aware of this order of his and the containing provisions?

utterances.speaker: OBREN PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it's been a long time, but from what I can see, that's it.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, if the OTP has no objection to make, the witness is familiar with the document and was aware of, and I wish to tender it into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Mr. Cvijetic, I eventually appreciated that the previous document was being tendered in support of the Defence case that the curfew was of universal application and wasn't confined to non-Serbs. I am not sure I appreciate what this document adds, why we would need to exhibit this. Could you assist me, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, this is another document that I'm using to show how restrictive the measure was that it even applied to policemen who could only move about the town if they had an appropriate written order to that effect, issued by their superiors. So I'm seeking to tender this to show the strict nature of the measure concerned. This other document, therefore, has its value independently as well, and not just as supplementing the earlier document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: We, by majority, rule that it may be admitted and marked.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit 1D261, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Mr. Cvijetic, I have a question in relation to adjudicated facts. The evidence you're eliciting from the witness about the curfew being applicable to everybody, is this a challenge of adjudicated fact 1268? Sorry, 12 -- yes, 1268. Is it?

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. And this isn't the first witness through whom we have been challenging this fact. I believe it's the third, in fact.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Well, but this -- the order -- or the dispatch you're referring to is of the 12th of September, if I'm not wrong; is that right?

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes [Microphone not activated].

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: And the date in the adjudicated fact is the 3rd of May of 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, the earlier document was dated in May. The Crisis Staff decision bears the date of May, and ... the 15th of May. Can you see it? I'm talking about the earlier document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: I can't see that. You have to help me.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 1D00-700.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Just for the record, that document is dated the 15th of June, not 15th of May. I know it refers to another decision of the 15th of May, but the header indicates 15th of June. Right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: But, Mr. Cvijetic, I still don't understand. The question that was raised by Judge Delvoie was whether a document which is dated the 12th of September, 1992, was introduced to challenge the adjudicated facts 1268, which refers to a situation taking place on the 3rd of May, 1992. So there seems to be a difference in time here of several months. So I'm not sure that I agree with you that the document from September could challenge the situation that was existing in Doboj in early May 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I agree with you in part, Your Honour. I said that this document has its independent value, regardless of all the earlier documents and the imposition of curfew. However, curfew was a standing measure that apparently was in force in September as well. This document indicates how the measure was implemented and who it applied to. That's the gist. And all of these documents taken together will indicate the continuity of the measure of curfew, imposition of measures to punish violations; and when we put all these documents together, they will lead us to a conclusion about the character of curfew and the way it was applied. I've already explained the basis on which I wish to tender this document into evidence. It has its independent value. The witness commented on it. It relates to his station and his centre.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: I accept -- I accept this. But in all fairness to the witness, I think that you would then have to go through the same exercise that we did earlier on with another witness, to check whether these laissez-passers or documents were issued to all citizens or only to Serbs. I mean, you remember the discussion we had at the time. And if you want to use this document as a means to challenge the adjudicated fact, then I think you -- you have to -- to do it thoroughly.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I will seek assistance from the witness, and I will put questions to him directly.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Mr. Petrovic, at the time the curfew was not in force, could all the citizens of Doboj municipality, regardless of their ethnicity, move freely about the town?

utterances.speaker: OBREN PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not when the curfew was in force.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: My question concerned the hours outside of the curfew.

utterances.speaker: OBREN PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. They could move freely when the curfew was not in force, but that was only for a short period of time.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Outside the curfew, were they required to carry along any sort of laissez-passers?

utterances.speaker: OBREN PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not initially, and this relates to the period right after the 3rd of May, the dates that the -- His Honour referred to. It was on the 4th and 5th and 6th. During this earlier period, people were taken into custody. It was only later on that the curfew was introduced and nobody could move about, and only those could move about who had special laissez-passers. They were Serbs, Croats, Muslims who were charged with essential services, who worked on special duties.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Therefore, when the curfew was in force, those who had permits, appropriate permits, be they Muslims, Croats, or Serbs, they could move about the town freely; is that right?

utterances.speaker: OBREN PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, they could.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: The part where you said who worked was not entered.

utterances.speaker: OBREN PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Who worked for specific companies and were under a work obligation.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Does -- Your Honour, does this answer your question?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Yes. I guess the issue boils down to the question of whether, to the witness's knowledge, there was, at any time, a situation in which laissez-passers or similar documents were handed out only to Serbs and not to Croats and Muslims in Doboj.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Mr. Petrovic, are you aware of such a situation as described by His Honour?

utterances.speaker: OBREN PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When this practice of issuing permits or laissez-passers started - I don't know when it was - they were issued to the Serbs because most of the Serbs were indeed manning the army and the police. To the Bosniaks, those who worked in companies, they were also issued with laissez-passers, as were Croats. If these individuals were not engaged in any such duties, they were not issued with laissez-passers.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Thanks.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Petrovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would, therefore, like to have this document admitted into evidence. Can we have a ruling on this? I'll repeat the number, 1D00-

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... it's admitted.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Okay. [Interpretation] Very well. Can we now call up document 1D00-0251.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Mr. Petrovic, we have a regular combat report of the command of the 1st Krajina Corps which was sent to the Main Staff of the Army of the Serbian Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina. Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: OBREN PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Military information is listed therein, describing the situation at the front lines, and this isn't something of interest to me. What I find relevant is the last page of the document.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we have that. It's page 3 in the B/C/S version, and, of course, the last page in the English. We need the earlier page in English. We'd like to see item 9. I see we don't have the last page in the B/C/S. Can we have items 9 in both versions. Yes, and have the English scrolled down. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Mr. Petrovic, the 1st Krajina Corps command states as follows, and I'm reading the second sentence: One police battalion has joined the Doboj Operational Group in keeping with your order. They reported on the afternoon of the 11th June. Mr. Petrovic, this seems to confirm what you said; that's to say, that we have an order of the Main Staff of the Serb army no less, whereby a police battalion was attached to the Doboj Operational Group. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: OBREN PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Can I explain?

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: I will put a question to you, so we'll get to that. Can you briefly tell me, what happens when such a police unit joins a military one? What becomes of the unit and its members? Can you explain this.

utterances.speaker: OBREN PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They are subordinated --

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Go ahead.

utterances.speaker: OBREN PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They are subordinated to military units. In this case, it involved preparations for breaching the corridor or breaking through the corridor, which means that they practically subordinated the entire Doboj police unit for the purposes of breaking through the corridor. Their justification for it was, I suppose, that the line along the centre of Doboj was one kilometre long, so they probably thought that by this token Doboj was part of the combat zone, and the police needed to get involved in these war operations. That was their explanation from the start.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: I think that what you said was that the entire police force in Doboj became part of this military unit manning the Doboj lines; is that right? Go ahead.

utterances.speaker: OBREN PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In this case, the entire police force was engaged, because it had to do with the opening up of the corridor. And I spoke also of individual cases where, depending on the operation, they would be engaging a company.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: The battalion, as well as the police officer in -- presumably in command of it, joined a military unit?

utterances.speaker: OBREN PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Bosko Djukic was at the head of this unit and led the unit in this particular assignment.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Do you know to which military commander he was resubordinated, if you know?

utterances.speaker: OBREN PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I don't know. I know that he was in the staff where the commander was Alic, but I don't know which brigade that was.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Can you please confirm that you are familiar with this order and that you're familiar with the resubordination, because the entire police force of Doboj was involved.

utterances.speaker: OBREN PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do know of resubordination. I don't know of the order itself, but I do know at the time of the corridor the entire force was resubordinated.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I would like to tender this document into evidence, unless this is an objection, because the witness knows enough about the contents of the document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Again, I'm not sure I see why.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, we have discussed with the witness - the witness volunteered information as well - about the conditions in Doboj at the time, what may have caused such conditions. He talked about how it was impossible to carry out regular police work in town itself at the time when combat operations were in progress. This document confirms, to a degree, his claims and explains them further.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: But as I understand, even when you're putting this document to the witness, you were dealing with one phrase in a lengthy document which, as I understand your questions, are -- are -- you find some assistance in, but I -- I don't see how the document is sufficiently relevant for our purposes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: And the witness doesn't know about this particular document. He knows about this -- the situation of subordination, but he doesn't know about this particular document.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I'll be accepting your suggestion, and I'll change my proposal. I would like to ask for this document to be marked for identification, because one of the coming witnesses will be a military expert and then we'll use him to give a comment on the document in its entirety. And as far as this element which related to the police, I think it was useful to have this witness comment on it, and I would tender it into evidence but marked for identification, please. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: So marked.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit 1D262, marked for identification, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Let us move to the next document, 1D00-2363, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Mr. Petrovic, what we see here is the reaction by the chief of the CSB to the issue of use of police in combat activities. He's practically protesting against it with the operation group command. He is asking for the withdrawal of the police from combat operations because the security situation in the Serbian municipality of Doboj, Derventa, Modrica is poor, which can be seen through increase of serious crimes such as murders, robberies, and similar. And then, in the second paragraph, he points out who is responsible for such crimes: conscripts, uniformed personnel. And makes a proposal that civilian police should coordinate with military police in order to suppress the crime. Can you see this?

utterances.speaker: OBREN PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Are you aware of this initiative of your chief, whereby he wanted to withdraw the police from combat operation? Do you know that the minister also asked for -- for it?

utterances.speaker: OBREN PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I can see from the document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Mr. Cvijetic, there were two questions. I have had one answer. To which of the two persons [sic] does that answer apply?

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Sir, let me separate the two questions. Do you know if the attempts by your chief of centre aimed at withdrawing the police from combat operations; are you -- were you informed about that?

utterances.speaker: OBREN PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, most probably I was, but this was 18 years ago.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: This as a result of this document.

utterances.speaker: OBREN PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, from the document I can see that he had asked for the police to be withdrawn from combat operation, military operations.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: You, as the chief of public security station, did you support this initiative? Did you also need police officers to help you in carrying out your regular duties?

utterances.speaker: OBREN PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: From the very beginning we stressed that it's necessary for the police to do their part of the work.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Your requests were, therefore, built into this request by the chief.

utterances.speaker: OBREN PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think so.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: The second part of the question, as Judge Delvoie insisted, was: Did you also receive requests from the minister asking for a withdrawal of police from combat operations to carry out regular duties?

utterances.speaker: OBREN PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't remember that.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, as far as the initiative by the chief of centre, I believe that this witness gave enough verification of the document. I would like to ask for the document to be tendered into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Your Honours, could we ask where this document comes from. Because at the bottom of this document it seems to be a compilation, and we see a page 137. And this is repeated with a number of other documents that the Defence seek to show. So can we find out where this comes from.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: And to assist the Judges, perhaps if the usher could scroll down to the bottom of the B/C/S version.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, this document, as well as others that will follow, we've received from the team for investigation of war crimes based on our request dated 16 of October, 2007. We will submit this document to the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Well, if that's the case, it would be more appropriate to have the whole book, rather than just one page. It might be of assistance.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
