utterances.text: [Interpretation] We are already in correspondence with the OTP. We are attempting to put all the documents that we received from this team and put them on one list. We have a date for this document already.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honours, I'm not seeking to take over, but the document saga here, as you know, is a long running one between the Defence and us. The Defence can't extract one page from a book and then decline to give us the rest of the pages. We are formally now requesting that we be supplied with the whole book from which this is page 137.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: So we need take no action now even in terms of considering marking this until the -- the whole matter of how this -- the document of which this is a page is sorted out.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, if I may intervene. There is no book. I don't know where Ms. Korner came up with the -- with the suggestion that this is a book. Somebody wrote 137 on the document. I don't know what it stands for. I -- I really don't know what it stands for. We received the document on our request. We will provide the Prosecutor with the official request and the official document, how we received this document, from whom we received it, and than is the batch. And we are using this document with this witness, and we are offering it -- for it to be marked and admitted. There's no -- I don't understand what book are we talking about at all. But we can clarify this in the next break with our friends from the OTP.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Well, yes, Your Honours, I agree. We needn't take this further, but it's no good in saying we received it with page 137; if that's right, where are the other 136? In what form was this document received? And, yes, can we see the original, please. And at this stage I think it would be safer - can I put it this way, Your Honour - were this document only to be marked MFI.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: If that would simply matters, yes, it would be so marked. And perhaps the -- I may have added confusion by using the -- by adding the term "book." But it seems -- I take Mr. Zecevic's point that he can only deal with what he has been given. And it's merely a -- once the communication is sorted out between both sides - and we -- we would all know where we are going forward for this - but, for the time being, the document will be marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Yes. One detail, Your Honours. The issue of the book. Can we scroll to the left of the B/C/S version. You can see that -- a bit more, please. You can see that it's a photocopy from a book. That's what was meant by "the book." Do you see, the page breaks. Yes. And so this is not an original document; it's a photocopy from a book, a compilation.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: So the exhibit will be 1D263, marked for identification, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May I continue, Your Honours?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Yes, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we have, please, document 1D00-2368.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Mr. Petrovic, what we have here is the response to the request issued by your chief where, in its second part, we can see a sentence saying the withdrawal of police is not authorised because, if I do so, the front will soon reach Doboj and you will not have any territory under your control. Can you see it?

utterances.speaker: OBREN PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: In his ultimate sentence, he says: "We welcome all forms of cooperation and assistance between the military police and the police forces." Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: OBREN PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: So, Mr. Petrovic, your chief obviously cannot withdraw the police from combat operations without authorisation of the military commander, and that can be seen from his answer?

utterances.speaker: OBREN PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Bearing in mind the comments from before, I will not tender -- I will not move to tender this document, only in the respect that it can be MFI'd maybe.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Your Honours, this is not a document that the document has seen. It does not emanate from the MUP. He cannot say how this document was drafted; we have the same objection about the source. But in addition to this, the witness can not recognise this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Unless I'm missing something, this seems to be a -- if not a part, a continuation of the previous document. Because as Judge Delvoie pointed out, the -- in the B/C/S version, the page number 138 appears at the bottom. It seems to be that -- for the same reasons that the previous document was marked for identification, that this would -- should similarly -- not should, could similarly be marked.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Could be marked, as long as we have that on the record.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit 1D264, marked for identification, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we have, please, document 1D01-0013.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Mr. Petrovic, your chief reacted by saying - and we can see that in paragraph 2 - that he was surprised by the content of the order. And then in the second paragraph you will find the sentence where it is stated: "Well, I was issuing for approval -- when I was issuing approval for engagement of police in combat without my consent or an order by the minister of the interior, there was looting and disorder behind the lines." And we then see a list of things that were taking place. Can you see this?

utterances.speaker: OBREN PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: As we can see here, your chief keeps on insisting on withdrawal of police from combat operations, but it doesn't seem to have effect.

utterances.speaker: OBREN PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It seems so.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In accordance with your ruling, we can see here this is a string of documents, a correspondence between military command and the police. I would like to ask for this document to be MFI'd, the document that was -- originated in the CSB.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Mr. Cvijetic, can I ask - I can't see it on the screen - but is it page 139?

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Same caveat, same objection, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit 1D265, marked for identification, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Could we now see the following document, 1D00-0345.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Mr. Petrovic, this is an order of the group of operations to establish a mixed battalion, comprised of a company of military police, a company of police from Doboj and Teslic. We can see that this military order appoints Mr. Andrija Bjelosevic commander of the company, and his deputy is Lieutenant Stijepan Pepic. Can you see it?

utterances.speaker: OBREN PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: In paragraph 3 there is even a combat order to attack along an axis mentioned here. Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: OBREN PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: You'll agree with me when I say, won't you, that your chief seems to have re-worded for his activity to pull out the police by being mobilised and sent off to the front line. Is that your impression?

utterances.speaker: OBREN PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's my impression.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Do you know that he was drafted and sent to the front line with this unit and that he took part in combat activities?

utterances.speaker: OBREN PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember, but I can see here that this, indeed, happened.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Obviously you know nothing about this document, right?

utterances.speaker: OBREN PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I will not tender this document because it does not emanate from the CSB.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please see the following document, 1D00 --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Mr. Cvijetic, it's just a few seconds before the time for the break. Would you wish to reserve opening with this document until we return?

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I agree with you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Mr. Cvijetic, before you proceed, the Bench has two questions of you, one connected with the other. I'll raise -- I'll formulate the first question; then Judge Delvoie, the question that's connected with that. And my question is that inasmuch as the -- as we understand the case - and we use the word "case" to mean what both sides are saying - there is no dispute as to the fact of the subordination of the police to the military at some point, and then, of course, certain things that would logically flow from this. What is the utility of this series of documents which you seem to have telegraphed that there are more to come, because I think there were, like, three that we had marked for identification, and there are more to come, and how does this assist us? But before you formulate an answer to that, Judge Delvoie has a connected question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: My question is about the adjudicated facts. As you may have noticed, I try to follow what is adjudicate and so on, and the Trial Chamber would very much appreciate it, very much be assisted, if you challenge an adjudicated fact, that you say so, that you announce the fact that are you challenging an adjudicated fact. That would be very helpful. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honours, before Mr. Cvijetic answers, can I just deal -- I'm taking over because this is a more general question connected with the case as a whole. To deal with the first question. Your Honours, the Prosecution's case is there is resubordination in times of combat. The Defence case as we understand it is that wherever the military are there's resubordination to -- by the police -- of the police to the military. We do not accept that. That is a bone of contention. And a major bone of contention. The second matter is this. We did many eons ago now say that the Defence should be required, once adjudicated facts were granted or when we thought they were granted, to say in -- not just as it comes up but which ones they were actually going to dispute by way of evidence, and we suggest that's something that should happen. Because as it is coming out piecemeal in this way, we don't know what evidence we've got to call to deal with what we assumed were adjudicated facts and accepted. But under the Lukic decision, as you know, at the last moment it transpired that the Defence were challenging adjudicated facts and the Prosecution were not allowed to the call evidence to deal with it. And so as His Honour Judge Delvoie says, I don't think it's good enough simply as it comes up for the Defence to say, We're challenging it, as has happened at the moment. We've got to know, literally, by the end of this month because clearly we are going to have to file - and we're working on it at the moment - matters -- sorry, an application to call evidence about matters which are no longer the subject of adjudicated facts. So from that point of view, may I say Judge Delvoie's point is a good one, but I think it has to go further than letting us know as it happens.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Thank you. Unless Mr. Cvijetic thinks that he has been ambushed, having been made aware of the Trial Chamber's concerns, this is something that he would consider, and we -- we could expect a considered response in the not-too-distant future. Could the witness be escorted back to the stand, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I don't feel ambushed in any way, and I accept your suggestion about announcing the challenging of adjudicated facts. And there's no problem about that -- with that. As for the legal relevance of the issue of resubordination, no comment of mine is required now because Ms. Korner has spoken about that. We represent opposed parties, and we must present evidence to support our case.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, before I start -- continue examining the witness, I would like to inform you that we have, in the meantime, procured a document of the cabinet of Republika Srpska date 16 October 2007 in which they reply to our request. And in that document, under numbers 77, 78, and 79, these very documents are listed which were marked for identification, because we could not prove their origin. And I will read which -- which documents these are. The documents are: 1D263, MFI; 1D264, MFI; and 1D265 MFI. And this document we received from the cabinet was also forwarded to the OTP. Therefore, it is our submission that these documents no longer have MFI status but, rather, be admitted as Defence exhibits.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Your Honours, there are two matters here. First of all, yes, we did receive a letter, but it's in Cyrillic. So at this moment I cannot read this document. But on a good-faith basis, I assume this was received from the Government of Republika Srpska or one of their organs. So once I am able to read it, I will be able to give you further submissions. That's number one. Number 2. It's not that we're saying there is any misconduct or misbehaviour on the part of the Defence in relation to the document; what we are saying is really that the source of the document itself seems to be of a dubious character. It seems to be coming from a photocopies of a book or compilation; I don't know. What we're interested in knowing is: Where is the original? Because this seems to be a photocopy of an original. And we don't know if the original exists. We don't know if the original has been tampered with or not. We don't know what it is exactly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Before Mr. Cvijetic answers, could I just get back to the contention that was raised by Ms. Korner, because I'm not sure I fully understood the gist of it. Ms. Korner is quoted as having said that the Prosecution's case is that there is resubordination in times of combat; whereas the Defence case is that there's resubordination by the police of the police to the military wherever the military is. I'm not sure I understand fully the -- the difference of this point of contention. I would like the parties to clarify.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Does Your Honour want to hear from me or Mr. Cvijetic on this?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Both of you.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I'll come around so that I can hopefully ... Your Honours, as I understand the Defence case, and it's one of the problems -- of course, and it wasn't spelled out anywhere before this case started, but it has been emerging through --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Would the counsel please speak into the microphone.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I'll come forward, Your Honours. As has been put to the witnesses is that if the military are stationed in an area, regardless of whether it is a front line, in other words there is actual fighting going on of any sort, the police are resubordinated to the military. If I'm wrong, then I have no doubt that Defence counsel will correct me. In other words, they are obliged to follow the orders issued by the military, completely overriding their own chain of command within the police. That is, as I understand it, the Defence. And that's where --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Regardless of any combat taking place in the area?

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Exactly. That is -- that is my understanding of the Defence case as it has been put. Regardless of whether there is combat going on, actual fighting between opposing forces, once the military is in an area, the police line of authority is subordinated to the military. And that is where the major disagreement comes. We say the only times that the police are resubordinated to the military - and we say that's what the evidence shows, regardless of what's being put by the documentation - is in times of actual combat, fighting, where police units are taken along -- up to the military. And if I'm wrong on that, then I think the Defence out to correct this now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Mr. Cvijetic or Mr. Zecevic, would either one of you wish to reply.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, the law is clear on this. First, under international conventions and regulations, after the state of -- imminent threat of war or the state of war have been proclaimed, the entirety territory of Republika Srpska has become a combat zone.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: He should explain what the position is, but he is giving evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm trying to state my position, but I'm being interrupted. My position is that the entire Republika Srpska was a combat zone. That means that all police officers who get orders to carry out a military task from a military commander in any part of the territory of the RS are resubordinated to the military command. That is our position. And that's in accordance with the law and the conventions.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: And in addition to what my learned friend said, especially in light of the fact of the imminent state of war which was declared, mid-of April and confirmed on 12th of May, 1992, at the Assembly session in Banja Luka. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: But can I just offer a third interpretation here. I have not discussed this with my colleagues, so I'm speaking clearly and truly and only on my own behalf now, and that is that it was my understanding that resubordination of -- of police forces to the armed force could take place upon a request from the army; but short of any such request, the police continued its activities. Whether or not there was combat activities in the area, if the army didn't request re-enforcement by police forces, then there was no resubordination. And as I understand it, there were sometimes situations in which the army was strong enough and didn't need it, didn't need support from the police and therefore didn't ask for it. And where the police wasn't asked to resubordinate any of its forces, the police force remained intact in the area. Is this misunderstood? And if it is, then I would wish to have it clarified right away. Hold on a minute.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honour, may I just say, the witness, of course, is sitting here. I don't know whether this is going to impact on cross-examination, but he ought to take his earphones off.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Mr. Petrovic --

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: -- would you be good enough to take your earphones off.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: No, but -- see, that wouldn't help. Of course, Mr. Cvijetic is speaking in the native language of the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Speak in English.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Mr. Cvijetic, I think that both parties have made their case -- have stated their case, and maybe this is not the correct moment to go in any further detail with this matter. So I suggest that we proceed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: If I may return to Mr. Demirdjian's two points. The second, as I recall it, in terms of the quality, for want of a better word, of the material on which the Defence is relying, to repeat what I would have said earlier, Mr. Zecevic, Mr. Cvijetic, can only deal with what they have. And there was a photocopy of some unknown -- the -- that may, at the end of the day, go to what weight would be attached to it because of the -- of any doubt that may be cast on its authenticity. So the -- so that second point is not one that would cause -- that should cause any pause in terms of the ability of the Defence to make use of this. As for the first point, of course, it must necessarily follow that until the documents are interpreted -- are translated so that the Prosecution can formally state their position, then they must remain marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honour, can I -- I'm sorry to keep coming back to this, but it is of some importance. For reasons I needn't trouble Your Honours with, we've given certain information to the Defence about one of their documents. Your Honours, our concern is this: This is -- and I know Your Honours - His Honour Judge Harhoff doesn't like it much - but it's a document case. Most of our -- our evidence is -- is documentary. It's therefore important that if documents come into evidence, either side is able, as far as is possible, to establish the provenance of the document. What is happening here -- Mr. Zecevic, of course, is perfectly entitled to ask any time for us to show where our documents come from, and we're always prepared to do that. Most of the documents have been used in other cases, so it hasn't arisen. Some of the documents that are appearing now have never appeared before in any other case. It's vital, we would submit to Your Honours, that the Defence make proper inquiries of their investigator or of the centre for Serbian war crime -- for investigation into war crimes against Serbs or for -- from -- from the MUP as to what the original of a document is. At the moment, they cannot tell us.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: In so far as they could.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: The --

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: But they're not telling us, Your Honour. They're simply saying, My investigator got it. And they have a duty, we would submit -- or if it comes from the war crimes centre, to say, if this is clearly as it is, three pages from a book, what is the original book, and can we see the rest of it. And they're not doing that. And, Your Honours, we say that's why we're objecting, at the moment, to these documents being anything other than marked for identification, whether or not they've got translations.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: I follow that, Ms. Korner. The -- I confess that before the -- I became involved in this matter, the idea of items, quote/unquote, falling off the back of a truck was limited to a certain type of criminal case. But it appears that many of the documents fall in that category, and we just have to see where we go.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour, can I -- I have said this over and over again, and -- but that's my objection at the moment to -- to some of these documents.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I apologise, but I really have to respond to this. Your Honour, I think that the comments from the Prosecution are, to put it mildly, unfair. The Prosecution is well aware that the sources we draw upon in preparing our Defence and the sources where we get the documents are very limited. I have neither the possibility or authority or staff, nor do any of other -- of the other members of the Defence team, to approach an official agency and ask them about the source of a document. I approached an official agency which has the authority to provide me with documents. I receive documents from this agency and rely upon them as authentic documents. It is, of course, up to me to decide whether I'm going use them and whether they support my case or not, but any investigation that would go further than that is something that I have neither the intention nor the power of doing. If Madam Korner finds the sources of the documents that we have suspicious and she has the list of all these sources, let her approach the relevant official agencies and inquire after the sources. This is absolutely not the task of the Defence. And I'm absolutely opposed to this. Specifically, Your Honour, most of the documents we have come from the Prosecution, including the document that Madam Korner referred to herself a moment ago. This is a document we received from the Prosecution. The document that she provided us with yesterday with comments on them already has an MFI number. We are now in a situation where I am supposed to be suspicious even of the documents I receive from the Prosecution. If this is the case, Your Honour, then we will be going through such situations on a daily basis. Every time a document is produced by either of the parties, we will have to inquire after the origin of the document, and this will lead us nowhere. I really did not have reason to suspect that all these documents that the Prosecution obtained were indeed documents that could be relied upon, but the same is true of the Defence. The Defence does not have the resources, possibilities, or staff to verify the authenticity of these documents or their sources. If this should be done, however, then we will have to go back to the beginning of the case.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... submission our learned friend Mr. Zecevic.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I'm sorry, but -- I know this is distracting from where we ought to be going, but, Your Honours, it's not incumbent upon the Prosecution to do the investigations. It's the Defence who are inviting Your Honours to rely on the truth and accuracy and provenance of these documents. It is their obligation to make sure that that is catered for if we raise a query. Now, most time, we don't; but every now and again, we do. And this particular book is one of them. And I'm not going to go into the document Mr. Zecevic has referred to. It's not one of our documents. It does bear a Prosecution number because by - I won't say by mistake - but because it was referred to by the Prosecution by the -- I'm sorry, by the Defence and didn't get a number. We had it marked for identification. But, Your Honours, that's a separate matter which may need further discussion. But as the general principle of the matter, if the Defence want documents admitted and the Prosecution raise a query, it is their obligation to be able to provide the information as to the actual source and whether or not it is authentic. Because they're the people that are asking you to rely on the documents.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Thank you. To bring this matter to an end, it seems to me that - and I speak entirely for myself - that the -- what I understand the position of the Defence now to be is that they have the certificate - my word - of the cabinet of the -- of the -- of the country -- of the city of origin of this, that that is as far as they can reasonably be expected to go. So -- sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: So everything is marked for identification -- remains marked for identification at this point. Please continue with your cross-examination, Mr. Cvijetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we call up -- or can we call up the next document which is 1D00-0343.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Mr. Petrovic, this is yet another order from Colonel Lisica where elements of the police force are sought to be resubordinated. One hundred policemen from the Doboj force are being requested. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: OBREN PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: They are issued with a combat assignment. And under 3 it is stated he shall hold a person responsible for this order, the chief, Andrija Bjelosevic, and you, yourself, sir. Do you know of this order?

utterances.speaker: OBREN PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I see it now.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Mr. Petrovic, what would happen if you and Mr. Bjelosevic simply disregarded the order or refused to implement it? What would happen?

utterances.speaker: OBREN PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We would be arrested.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Who would arrest you?

utterances.speaker: OBREN PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The military police of Colonel Lisica.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Let us recall the Criminal Code, pursuant to which refusal to carry out a military order in a state of a declared imminent threat of war is a serious offence, is it not?

utterances.speaker: OBREN PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, knowing Colonel Lisica as I do, whatever the law said, we would end up in prison.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Sir, since this order refers, among others, also to the witness present here, in accordance with the earlier position you stated, can we have this document marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit 1D266, marked for identification, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Mr. Petrovic, the last document of the batch, which I want to use merely to confirm what you said about the partial resubordination of the police force.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is document 1D00-0332.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Mr. Petrovic, in this order, Colonel Lisica dispatches a unit of the Doboj police to a battle-field in the area of another municipality, i.e., Derventa. Please have a look at this. And they are to join the Bosanski Brod Battalion. Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: OBREN PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Under item 4, again, the responsibility for the implementation of order lies with the centre and the public security station [as interpreted]. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: OBREN PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: So from one zone, the zone of Doboj, this unit is dispatched to another zone, wherever needed, wherever they're needed to carry out military assignments. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: OBREN PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I'd like to move for this document to be MFI'd for the very same reasons as with the previous one.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Despite the -- having trod this well-worn path now, Mr. Cvijetic, I'm wholly unable to appreciate how this, in any way, assists the issue. Isn't this just another piece of paper that we're adding to the pile? I ... This particular document really seems, to me, to be beyond the pale. If you could show me how this falls in the same category as the previous documents that we marked for identification ...

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, pursuant to orders by the military commander, a battalion is established attached to Bosanski Brod. Bosanski Brod is a municipality that's outside of the Doboj area. Police is being sent there to carry out military assignments. All this as a part of a claim concerning a combat zone. And what we are claiming is that the Republika Srpska immediately after the proclamation of immediate threat of war has become a combat zone in its totality. And military organs were able to send police units to carry out military combat assignments in any part of Republika Srpska. This order had to be obeyed, and the sanctions, if it wouldn't be, were very strict.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Very well. So marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit D1D267, marked for identification, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Your Honour, one item for the transcript. I don't know if this is a problem with translation, but page 66, line 2, is recorded that Mr. Cvijetic said: "Under item 4, again, the responsibility for the implementation of the order lies with the centre and the public security station." Now, the document at item 4 does not say "public security station." From the English translation that I have in front of me, it says "the chief of Doboj region, public security service." I don't know if there is a problem with either translations. Maybe it can be clarified.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Mr. Cvijetic, perhaps -- I don't -- I don't myself see the difference, the mere change of -- difference between "service" and "station." But to the extent that it may be relevant, perhaps Mr. Cvijetic may wish to have the witness speak -- speak to this.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It's very simply, Your Honours. The colonel used an improbable word where he is using -- or formula where he is implying both the service and the stations. He is saying Mr. Bjelosevic, who is chief of public security service, although Mr. Bjelosevic was chief of centre. And that got me wrong-tracked. I do agree with the Prosecutor. He was referring to the centre only, but it was typed wrongly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ...

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Mr. Petrovic, before I show you some further orders that -- that had been sent from the CSB Doboj to you by chief of centre, Andrija Bjelosevic, and before we go through the reports drafted by the inspectors and the persons sent from the Ministry of Interior for the purpose of verifying the situation in the Doboj centre and station, I would like to go, rather quickly, through a few orders by the minister of the interior so that we would be able to understand the requests that were sent and the orders aimed at removing the shortcomings in the area covered by the CSB. Thus --

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we have, please, document 1D76.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Please read this order. You've been asked already about this meeting held on the 11th of July in Belgrade. You told us, if I'm not mistaken, that you don't know anything about it.

utterances.speaker: OBREN PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: After the meeting or the collegium, the minister, based on information received from the ground, drafted this order asking for information concerning the activities of paramilitary formations. You can find that under small (a). Then under (b), data and information regarding police involvement in combat operations. We have covered this second topic extensively today.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like to ask to move to the following page in both versions, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Furthermore, information related to prevention and detection of crimes. Then information concerning collection camps. Then operation of military judiciary authorities, and so forth. I assume you're not familiar with this order?

utterances.speaker: OBREN PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember it.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: But you could have found out about the assignments stated in this order only after the members of the Ministry of Interior managed to physically enter the place where they were stored. You were shown the transcripts yesterday by the Prosecutor. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: OBREN PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: I would like to show to you another order by the minister.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It's 1D49.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: As you can see, this order is dated 23rd of October. In item number 1, the minister orders all active-duty police members to withdraw from combat operations and the reserve police force members to be made available. Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: OBREN PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Item number 2 will later on be of interest to us. The minister is here ordering that the number of the reserve police force members be reduced and that it should be 1:2 ratio. Can you see that? And then the excess, to call it like that, of reserve police members to be put at the disposal of the VRS?

utterances.speaker: OBREN PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can see that.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: In second paragraph of item number 2, the minister even authorises chiefs to inform the military commands that they are no longer obliged to provide police force members for participation in combat operations, except in municipalities which are directly affected by combat activities. Can you see that in the second paragraph?

utterances.speaker: OBREN PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Later we'll be discussing the documents that did reach you, where you were asked to reduce the number of reserve police members. Do you remember receiving such documents?

utterances.speaker: OBREN PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think so.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Let me show you another order by the minister.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 1D76. 176. I don't know whether this is the document. No, this is an earlier document. Yes, this one.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: This order dated 27th of July, 1992, in item number 1, the minister asks for the optimal number of members of security services to be determined based on the criteria prescribed by the Law on Internal Affairs and the rules mentioned in the document. And in item number 2, he recalls an earlier order of his, asking for all those who have committed crimes and/or are criminal investigations instigated against them to be removed from the force. Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: OBREN PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [No verbal response]

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Three, then there is discussion about this surplus of police forces to be put at the disposal of the army. And under 4, he is asking for all special units formed during the war in areas of Security Services Centres to be disbanded and placed under the command of the Army of the Serbian Republic? Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: OBREN PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: In this same item, we can see that a detachment of the ministry police was established in the centre and that all those interested and all those who meet the criteria may apply for membership in the organisation. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: OBREN PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: On the following page --

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we have the following page, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Item 7, the minister orders that all paramilitary formations should be removed from the areas that are not under the control of the Army of the Serbian Republic. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: OBREN PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: And in the subsequent items, he reiterates his positions about the modes of police work. Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: OBREN PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: This order reached you, again, indirectly, through orders issued by the chief of the CSB and through the persons from the ministry who came to carry out the control. I assume you remember some of these elements?

utterances.speaker: OBREN PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We received this order through the chief of the centre.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I'll show you another order.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 1D55.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: This order is something whereby the minister prescribes the detention of holding people in custody of three days. He is stating that this must be done exclusively within the regulation prescribed, and prohibits any misuse. Also, describing how the premises where these people would be detained should look like. It's under 1. You can see that, don't you -- can't you?

utterances.speaker: OBREN PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Two, the security of collection centres shall be the direct responsibility of the Serbian army, and if they do not have enough men for these duty, the members of reserve police should be engaged. Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: OBREN PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Mr. Petrovic, we've been through just -- several of these orders with the intention of making it easier to understand some of the documents from your areas and the reasons of their adoption. I would like to show you now a document from your area, issued by your station.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It's 1D03-3159. I'm waiting for the English version. Is this document maybe still waiting for the translation? Oh, there is a translation.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May I continue, Your Honours?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ...

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Mr. Petrovic, on page 1, I think I see your signature. There's your name.

utterances.speaker: OBREN PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Is it your signature?

utterances.speaker: OBREN PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Is it your document?

utterances.speaker: OBREN PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Let us comment on it. You are referring to a document you received from the CSB on the 6th of October, 1992. Can you see it? And you are requested that you should see to it that the reserve police stations should start functioning, and you informed the centre that did you so.

utterances.speaker: OBREN PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Let us move on to the following page to see how you did it. Mr. Petrovic, you were saying yesterday that in the case of war or in imminent threat of war, reserve police stations are established in some parts of the municipality, right?

utterances.speaker: OBREN PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: That was -- there were provisions to that effect in military rules and regulations and police rules and regulations, even before the war, right?

utterances.speaker: OBREN PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: And that -- such provisions were also to be found in the rules and regulations of the Republika Srpska, right?

utterances.speaker: OBREN PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Yesterday you explained that Major Stankovic turned all these stations into detachments to be able to use them for military purposes. Did I understand your explanation that you gave yesterday correctly?

utterances.speaker: OBREN PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: You will agree with me when I say, won't you, that this detrimentally affected the organisation of the MUP, the way it was envisaged by the rules and regulations; correct?

utterances.speaker: OBREN PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: This was noticed on the occasion of a check carried out by the MUP, and you received the task to adapt the actual situation to the law.

utterances.speaker: OBREN PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: And it follows from this document that you actually did that, right?

utterances.speaker: OBREN PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: This document of yours basically says that the organisation established by Major Stankovic, that is, the existence of detachments, should cease to exist and that the orders should go from the CSB, in accordance with the existing rules and regulations, right?

utterances.speaker: OBREN PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I believe that there can be no doubt about this. This is a document which emanates from the witness, and I believe it can be admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Admitted and marked.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Your Honours, I do have one comment in relation to Mr. Cvijetic's last sentence. Page 75, line 2, says that this document says that the organisation established by Major Stankovic, that is, the existence of detachments, should cease to exist. Although this could be clarified by the witness, I don't agree that the document says that. The document only establishes the reserve police stations. So just for the interpretation of this document ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Well, I don't know that we need become entangled in that because the document says what it says. And no doubt at the end of the exercise submissions and arguments will be made as to what the effect of the contents of the document. So the witness's -- what counsel puts to a witness about what a document says is of minimal use in that regard.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: So the document will be Exhibit 1D268, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. I will now move on to the following document, which is 1D01-0341.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Before you move on, Mr. Cvijetic. Returning to Mr. Demirdjian's intervention, I suppose I should add to what I would have said, that it is entirely possible and proper for counsel to put to a witness what his understanding of the document was, even if it appears to be at variance with what was on the face of document, especially where in this case the witness would have himself acted on the basis of his understanding, which doesn't seem to have arisen here. But I just wanted to modify and clarify my general observation earlier. Yes, Mr. Cvijetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours. That would have been my remark, but I didn't have time to reply to the Prosecutor.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Mr. Petrovic, this is a document from November 1992. It is signed by the chief of the centre, Andrija Bjelosevic, and other centre staff with their respective positions indicated below. And in the introduction we see that it's an -- it's an activity plan of the department for police duties. Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: OBREN PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: What I'm interested in is item 1. It says that it must be established whether or not in organisational units of the centre there are members of the reserve police force who have not served in the military or who have a criminal file, except for crimes related to traffic safety and so on. Mr. Petrovic, this reminds you of one of those orders of the minister of the interior where he demands that it must be established whether or not some persons committed crimes, right?

utterances.speaker: OBREN PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, yes, I guess so. The centre probably was acting pursuant to orders from the minister.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we turn to the following page, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Here the inspector states that he did the job in November. And in paragraph 2 he says that he established the number of reserve police force members who had -- have not served in the military, as well as the number of those convicted of crimes which makes them not eligible for working for the Ministry of Interior. Can you see that in paragraph 2?

utterances.speaker: OBREN PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: On page 3, there's a list of these persons.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please show page 3.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: In the first section, there are those convicted of -- for crimes. And there are even references to the articles of the relevant laws and their verdicts. And in the latter section, there is a list of those who have not served in the military. Mr. Petrovic, this plan of work and these conclusions regarding the state of affairs, were they drafted in keeping with the instructions given by the minister of the interior?

utterances.speaker: OBREN PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe so.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: In other words, you mean that these orders were carried out?

utterances.speaker: OBREN PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I think so.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, this may be a convenient time to adjourn. Although, I have a document now which I might be able to finish in ten minutes. But I am in your hands, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Sorry, Ms. Korner, you have something to say on this point?

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Only if Your Honours are going to - I just wanted to mention - come back to adjudicated facts for a moment. I thought -- I didn't realise Your Honours were still considering Mr. Cvijetic's offer to stop now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated] ... said it would take about ten minutes --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Inasmuch as he says it would take about ten minutes to open on this new document, perhaps it would be advisable to take the adjournment now. And then we can deal with your point.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone for the Judge, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Sorry. Mr. Petrovic, we are to take the adjournment for today. Your cross-examination will continue tomorrow morning. We continue at 9.00 in this courtroom. The Court will not adjourn immediately. We have an administrative matter with -- housekeeping matter with which to deal. So the usher will now escort you from the courtroom. And I remind you what I said yesterday about not discussing the case. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Korner.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. Your Honours, I am a bit concerned -- and now that Judge Delvoie has seised the adjudicated facts as they are with such vigor, because we did raise it on the 12th of June, I have been reminded by Mr. Smith that during the Status Conference then I said that we're a bit concerned about the suggestion that seems to be happening at the moment that there is going to be a challenge to the adjudicated facts which have already been ruled on and which the Trial Chamber has accepted - or so we thought at the time, in parentheses. And in the light of the Lukic case, if there is to be such a challenge, perhaps that is something that ought to be indicated in the briefs submitted by the Defence so that we all know where we are. And Judge Harhoff said I would assume that to be raised by the Defence teams. Now, Your Honours, the reality is, like so many other things, it sort of disappeared into the general morass. But we would invite Your Honours, really, to make an order that such adjudicated facts as we have, if they are to be challenged, then we really ought to be told in writing by the Defence as soon as possible so that we know exactly where we are, everybody now knows what their case is. So we would really invite Your Honours to do that. That's the first thing. The second thing, can I deal --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Sorry. For my own edification, Ms. Korner, in previous cases has such a requirement been imposed on the side challenging adjudicated facts?

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I don't -- Your Honours, to be quite honest, I don't know. And -- but I think the first time that it actually emerged as an issue was in the Lukic case, which finished, I think, shortly before or after this case had already begun. So that -- Your Honours, to answer, I don't if that -- ever that's -- that's happened before, but I don't equally know whether once an adjudicated fact has been granted there's been this kind of challenge. So that's -- I mean, so the simple is, I don't know, but I can find out quite easily.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: You had a second point.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes, second point is simply on timing, Your Honour. Perhaps we could inquire of Mr. Cvijetic how much longer he is going to be, because on Monday we have a journalist testifying. He has just confirmed that. And his work schedule is such that he literally needs to start on Monday. And then we have a videolink witness on Wednesday, in any event, of next week. So I would quite like to know, because we've got another potentially two witnesses this week, how much longer Mr. Cvijetic is going to be. And then Mr. Pantelic or Mr. Krgovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I believe that I need one more session to finish with this witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, I don't think that we have any cross-examination for this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Would you like -- Your Honours, you would like me to answer the first point by Ms. Korner at this point or should I do that tomorrow?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Well, if you are able to speak to it briefly now, but we would understand that you would like to think about it.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Well, I can comment briefly on it, but if you want me to give you a bit complexed submission on this, I would do that, rather, tomorrow morning, if possible.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: I wouldn't have used the word "complex," myself; but I prefer to use the word "considered," because I appreciate that this is something that you would not have been alerted to beforehand and would be more useful if you have the opportunity to reflect on it for a few hours before you assist us with your suggestions in this regard.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much. I understand. And it is my English, because I used the word "complex," Your Honours, "considered" is a very appropriate word which I wanted to say. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Just for the record, Your Honours. The position of Zupljanin Defence regarding adjudicated facts is the following: We are challenging every single adjudicated fact. End of story. Just for the record. We don't want to make any other submission.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Pantelic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, just to make the Prosecutor's life easier, with regard to the witness that is about to come, we are sure to challenge each and every adjudicated fact from that -- from that testimony and the statement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: And so our path --

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Teslic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: And so our path is well laid out for us. Thank you. We now rise until tomorrow morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Wednesday, the 12th day of May, 2010, at 9.00 a.m.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 1.47 p.m.,
